what: A contact sensor changes the drive commands when the robot touches an obstacle. Contact feedback stops or reverses a moving robot.
try: Use the supplied example and obstacle mat. Reset and run.
Watch the touch reading when the bumper reaches the obstacle.
Compare contact-triggered reversal with the distance-triggered wall-stopper.
why: Contact feedback is an event at the bumper, followed by a programmed reaction. The location of the contact surface and sensor travel determine when the event happens.
matters: Bumpers are a simple way to detect a failed path or physical contact.
question: Can this contact sensor stop the robot before any physical contact occurs?
answer: No. It detects contact. Detecting an obstacle in advance requires a suitable non-contact sensor.
further: Compare the bumper’s position with the body front.
Experiment with a lower approach speed.
